figures.finding: Sint Maarten's own income and wage tax for 2026 runs 0% to Cg 21,200, then 12.5%, 20%, 26.25%, 33.75%, 40% and 47.5% from Cg 179,500, less a basic credit of Cg 2,381 (with further credits for sole earners, children and the elderly).
figures.applies: Income and wage tax, 2026 Deloitte's Sint Maarten Highlights 2026 prints other bands (12.5% to XCG 36,576 … 47.5% above 161,540); the Tax Administration's own 2026 table (quoted) is used.

figures.finding: Employers withhold wage tax from the 2026 period tables (basic credit built in); nothing is withheld where the monthly base is Cg 2,273.44 or less (Cg 27,281.28 a year), and pay above the end of a table bears 47.5%.

figures.finding: The employee's AOV/AWW old-age and survivors' premium is 6.5% of pay in 2026 (stated as provisional), deducted before wage tax.

figures.finding: The tax year is the calendar year (tables apply to pay periods from 1 January 2026).

figures.finding: SZV's latest published premium sheet puts AOV at 13% (employer 7%, employee 6%), AWW at 1% (0.5% each), ZV health at 12.5% (employer 8.3%, employee 4.2%) and OV accident at 0.5% to 5% by risk class (employer), plus a cessantia levy of NAf 40 per employee a year; ZV and OV stop at NAf 120,000 a year, and the 2026 AOV/AWW wage maximum is Cg 132,824.35.
figures.applies: Employees; the percentages and the ZV/OV ceiling are SZV's April 2024 sheet (no later percentage sheet is published; its 2026 sheet gives amounts and wage limits only), the AOV/AWW wage maximum is SZV's 2026 sheet. The employee AOV+AWW share (6% + 0.5%) matches the 6.5% in the 2026 wage-tax table.

figures.finding: A freelancer's fee bears turnover tax (BBO/TOT) at 5%; there is no turnover threshold: every entrepreneur registers and files monthly, even with nil turnover.
figures.applies: Resident and non-resident entrepreneurs supplying services in Sint Maarten. The Tax Administration's own TOT pages list documents client-side, so two tax firms are quoted; tax.sx's calendar confirms monthly returns due mid-month.

sources.said: Standard rate of 5% for realized revenues (on a cash basis) with the sale of goods or for providing services. … Any person that qualifies as an entrepreneur must register for TOT purposes and file monthly tax returns, even if the taxable turnover is nil.

Rates: The standard rate is 5%. Registration: Residents and nonresidents that make taxable supplies of goods or services in Sint Maarten must register with the tax authorities. … Filing and payment: A self-assessment regime applies and payment must be made monthly.

Business This section includes the Verzamelloonstaat, Opgave Derden, requests for reduced or postponed filings, the Turnover Tax Ordinance list, and more. … DEC 15 Monthly Tax Return - November 2026 Ensure your November 2026 Tax Return is filed & paid on time.

figures.finding: An income tax return is filed on the Inspectorate's invitation within two months of it (the 2025 returns were due 1 June 2026); a person not invited must request a return.

sources.said: Every natural person who receives worldwide income must file an income tax return with the Inspectorate of Taxes … You have two (2) months from the date of the invitation to file your tax return by completing and submitting the (paper) tax return form.

The Inspectorate of Taxes announces that the deadline to submit the 2025 Income Tax Return Forms A & B is June 1, 2026. Invitations to file the 2025 Income Tax Return are being sent by regular mail. Taxpayers who do not receive an invitation to file are obliged to request such.

figures.finding: A non-resident is taxed only on Sint Maarten-source income, at the resident scale on assessment; no withholding tax is levied on royalties or service fees, and no artiste-specific withholding is published.
figures.applies: Non-residents; the artiste rule is not modeled beyond this (see blocker).

sources.said: Basis: Sint Maarten residents are taxed on their worldwide income. Nonresidents are taxed only on Sint Maarten-source … There is no withholding tax on dividends, interest, royalties, or technical service fees in Sint Maarten
